title: Election participation depends on an administrative route from attempted ballot to counted ballot
source_unit: Election Assistance Commission 2024 Election Administration and Voting Survey; state and jurisdiction reports
geography: United States; all 50 states, District of Columbia, and five territories

observations.method: EAC compilation of state and local election-official responses in the biennial EAVS and companion policy survey.
observations.uncertainty: The report uses administrative reporting with state and jurisdiction definitions, casewise availability, and different provisional-ballot rules; rounded national summaries do not expose every local denominator.
observations.subgroup: States, territories, DC, local election jurisdictions, voting methods, and provisional-ballot outcomes.
observations.counterinterpretation: A provisional rejection may follow a valid rule or voter-cure boundary and does not alone establish wrongful exclusion; high participation and paper records can coexist with unequal access or low trust.

related_sources.claim: EAC publishes EAVS reports, datasets, codebooks, and policy-survey materials.
EAC's release summarizes 2024 participation, counted ballots, voting methods, and paper-record use.

boundary: This record measures state-reported election administration and ballot outcomes. It does not follow individual voters, establish equal access or improper rejection, measure persuasion or trust, or connect administration to later political action.
